outages.place: Southern Odisha, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Kandhamal, and Boudh
outages.affected: TPSODL, as reported by OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray on Nov 20, 2026, said it had restored electricity supply to 1,069,026 consumers (written as 10,69,026 in those reports) after Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur on Friday morning, achieving 98.68 percent restoration — nearly 99 percent — across its eight-district operational area within seven hours. Those reports said all six affected 33 kV feeders, all 19 affected 33/11 kV power substations, and all 42 affected power transformers were restored, and that 364 of 365 affected 11 kV feeders and 35,749 affected distribution transformers had been restored. District-wise restoration was reported as 99.76 percent in Ganjam, 99.53 percent in Koraput, 98.90 percent in Gajapati, 98.06 percent in Rayagada, 98.01 percent in Nabarangpur, 97.55 percent in Boudh, 94.23 percent in Kandhamal, and 100 percent in Malkangiri. TPSODL CEO Amit Kumar Garg, quoted in those reports, said the company had achieved nearly 99 percent restoration. An earlier Nov 20 Odisha Stand report from Berhampur said TPSODL had reported that Cyclone Akvan affected 1,083,348 consumers across its operational area, including 534,361 in Ganjam district and 123,252 in Nabarangpur district. Later Nov 20 articles, including Odisha News Online from Berhampur, described Garg visiting cyclone-affected areas of Ganjam to review restoration and restated the same 1,083,348 affected-consumer total, including the Ganjam and Nabarangpur district figures, but did not give a later remaining-outage count or a later restoration percentage after the 98.68 percent figure. No official remaining-outage count, and no official estimated time for full restoration of remaining customers, was stated in the later OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray reports. No later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL or the Odisha government was found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday.
outages.start: Morning of Nov 20, 2026 (IST), when Cyclone Akvan made landfall near Gopalpur
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, TPSODL figures via OdishaBytes and Odisha Ray (Nov 20); earlier TPSODL affected total via Odisha Stand (Nov 20); CEO restoration review via Odisha News Online (Nov 20), which restated the same affected total and did not give a later remaining-outage count; no later official remaining-outage count or official notice of full restoration from TPSODL or the Odisha government found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday

outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20
outages.affected: Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a statement reported by Ukrinform at 1:41 p.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (5:41 a.m. CT), said that during the night and morning Russia had launched another large-scale attack on critical energy infrastructure — power plants and substations of electricity transmission and distribution systems — and that nuclear power plants were forced to reduce their generation capacity. The ministry said a return to normal operating procedures would take place gradually after damaged networks were restored. As of Friday morning, the ministry said, some consumers remained without power in the city of Kyiv and in the Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kirovohrad, Odesa, Kharkiv, Kherson, Cherkasy, and Chernihiv regions. Ukrinform's English report described that list as "Kyiv and 11 regions" while naming those same 10 regions plus Kyiv; the named list is used here. The Energy Ministry said that to stabilize the power system, emergency outages were being implemented in the city of Kyiv and in the Lviv, Zakarpattia, Dnipropetrovsk, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Ivano-Frankivsk regions, and that a return to forecast hourly schedules would take place after the situation in the power system stabilized. It said two energy workers were injured in the Kharkiv region as a result of the attack and were taken to hospital. DTEK, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 2:35 p.m. EET Friday (6:35 a.m. CT), said energy workers had managed to stabilize the electricity-supply situation in Kyiv and return to planned outages after the emergency cuts applied following the overnight and morning attack. DTEK said in Telegram, as quoted by Interfax-Ukraine, that power had been returned to Kyiv residents and that outage schedules were then in effect in the capital. Ukrenergo, as reported by LB.ua at 6:43 p.m. EET Friday (10:43 a.m. CT) and by UNIAN at 7:18 p.m. EET Friday (11:18 a.m. CT), said that on Saturday, Nov 21, planned electricity outages would be in effect around the clock in parts of the country because of the aftermath of attacks on the power system. Ukrenergo said all categories of consumers would face hourly outage schedules of 1.5 to 3 groups, and that industry would face capacity-restriction schedules. UNIAN, citing Ukrenergo, said those 1.5 to 3 queues for household consumers should correspond to outages of 6 to 12 hours, and that the hourly schedules for the public and the industrial restrictions would both run throughout Saturday. Those Saturday schedules were in effect at the time of this update (2:00 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21, which is 6:00 p.m. CT Friday). DTEK, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 9:38 p.m. EET Friday (1:38 p.m. CT), said that during the night and morning Russia had launched more than 400 strike drones and more than 110 missiles at Ukraine, and that targets included power plants and substations. DTEK said Ukrainian nuclear power plants that had reduced output because of network damage would gradually increase power as networks were restored. It said that as of Friday morning, some consumers in Kyiv and ten regions had remained without power, including in Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa, and that in Kyiv power had already been returned and outage schedules were again in effect in the capital. No official nationwide customer count was given. An evening Friday recheck at 6:00 PM CT Friday found no official nationwide customer count.
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, DTEK via Interfax-Ukraine 9:38 p.m. EET Friday (= 1:38 p.m. CT) on the attack scale, nuclear plants, and Friday-morning regional status, and DTEK via Interfax-Ukraine 2:35 p.m. EET Friday (= 6:35 a.m. CT) on cancellation of emergency outages in Kyiv; Ukrenergo via LB.ua 6:43 p.m. EET Friday (= 10:43 a.m. CT) and UNIAN 7:18 p.m. EET Friday (= 11:18 a.m. CT) on Saturday Nov 21 all-day schedules, which were in effect at this update; Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (= 5:41 a.m. CT); rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday

outages.cause: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including a large-scale overnight and morning attack on Nov 20. DTEK said Friday morning that emergency outages were in effect in Dnipro city and in the Dnipro, Samarivka, Pavlohrad, and Kamianske districts, and that hourly schedules did not apply there. For Saturday, Nov 21, Ukrenergo and DTEK published all-day hourly (stabilization) outage schedules for the region
outages.affected: DTEK, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 10:26 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (2:26 a.m. CT), said at 8:47 a.m. EET Friday (12:47 a.m. CT) that emergency outages had been introduced in part of Dnipropetrovsk region, and that in Dnipro city and in the Dnipro, Samarivka, Pavlohrad, and Kamianske districts emergency outages were in effect and hourly schedules did not apply. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, as reported by Ukrinform at 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (5:41 a.m. CT), said that as of Friday morning some consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power, and that emergency outages were being implemented in Dnipropetrovsk region, among other regions, to stabilize the power system. DTEK, as reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 9:38 p.m. EET Friday (1:38 p.m. CT), again said that as of Friday morning some consumers had remained without power in Kyiv and ten regions, including Dnipropetrovsk. No official customer count for Dnipro or Dnipropetrovsk region was given in those Friday statements. Informator, citing Ukrenergo, reported that on Saturday, Nov 21, hourly outage schedules would be in effect in Dnipropetrovsk region throughout the day, from 12:00 a.m. to 11:59 p.m., and that 1.5 to 3 queues of consumers would be disconnected at the same time across Ukraine, with capacity restrictions for industry. Informator also published Saturday group-by-group schedules attributed to DTEK and to CEK for Dnipropetrovsk region. Those Saturday schedules were in effect at the time of this update (2:00 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21, which is 6:00 p.m. CT Friday). No later official statement was found confirming that the Friday emergency outages in Dnipro and the four districts remained in effect on Saturday after those schedules were published. No official customer count for the region was given in the Friday evening or Saturday-schedule reports. The latest official customer count found remains DTEK's Tuesday-morning figure. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17 report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power in Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named those districts. No official restoration time was given. No later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday.
outages.start: Morning of Nov 17, 2026 (Kyiv time), after earlier attacks on the evening of Nov 16
outages.updated: Nov 20–21, 2026, Ukrenergo and DTEK Saturday Nov 21 schedules via Informator; DTEK via Interfax-Ukraine 9:38 p.m. EET Friday (= 1:38 p.m. CT); DTEK via Ukrainska Pravda 10:26 a.m. EET Friday (= 2:26 a.m. CT), citing DTEK at 8:47 a.m. EET Friday (= 12:47 a.m. CT); Energy Ministry via Ukrinform 1:41 p.m. EET Friday (= 5:41 a.m. CT); Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure, DTEK via Suspilne and Censor.NET; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday, no later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure found

outages.cause: Russian attack on a DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi energy facility on the morning of Nov 20. DTEK's official evening statement also said weather-damage cleanup was continuing in the region
outages.affected: DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in an official Nov 20 evening statement titled "Situation with electricity as of the evening of November 20," said that after the morning enemy attack the situation in Odesa and the region remained controlled, that all critical-infrastructure facilities had been energized, that stabilization (scheduled) outage schedules were in effect, and that electricity was gradually returning to homes. It said repair work on energy facilities was continuing, and that power had been restored in part of the Odesa and Rozdilna districts after the morning shelling of substations. It said 8,000 families in 21 settlements remained without power, that temporary voltage drops were possible during the work, and that restoration was being made extremely difficult by continuous air-raid alerts in the region. The same official statement said weather-damage cleanup was also continuing in the region: during the day specialists had restored power for 37,700 families, and DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns. The company did not add the 8,000 and 15,600 figures together and did not announce a firm time for full restoration. Earlier Friday, 41,000 households were without power in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts, according to DTEK's press service as reported by Ukrainska Pravda at 11:27 a.m. EET Friday, Nov 20 (3:27 a.m. CT), and by Ekonomichna Pravda at 10:55 a.m. EET Friday (2:55 a.m. CT). Both reports said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 20 hit a DTEK energy facility, and that power engineers would begin inspecting surviving equipment, carrying out repairs, and resuming the electricity supply as soon as the security situation permits. Odesa regional military administration head Oleh Kiper, in a Friday Telegram post reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 10:26 a.m. EET Friday (2:26 a.m. CT), said that according to preliminary data there were no casualties, and that as a result of the attack more than 41,000 consumers in the Odesa and Rozdilna districts were temporarily without power. No later official remaining customer count after this official evening statement was found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday (2:00 a.m. EET Saturday, Nov 21).
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The official evening statement said repair work after the morning attack was continuing, and that crews would work overnight to restore power to another 15,600 families in 55 villages and towns (the weather-related figure in that statement). That is not an official firm time for full restoration.
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi official evening statement on remaining 8,000 families after the morning attack and on 15,600 families still to be restored overnight after weather damage; earlier Friday morning 41,000-household figure, DTEK press service via Ukrainska Pravda 11:27 a.m. EET Friday (= 3:27 a.m. CT) and Ekonomichna Pravda 10:55 a.m. EET Friday (= 2:55 a.m. CT); Oleh Kiper via Interfax-Ukraine 10:26 a.m. EET Friday (= 2:26 a.m. CT); rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday, no later official remaining count after the evening statement found

outages.place: Kurdistan Region, including Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Duhok, Bazian, and Chamchamal
outages.cause: Suspected drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field on the night of Nov 8, 2026, which halted gas production that supplies much of the region's electricity generation. Dana Gas, the field's operator, later said the facility had sustained significant damage and could produce no gas
outages.affected: Al Jazeera, on Nov 9, 2026, citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials, said a Sunday-night drone attack on the Khor Mor gas field caused a fire and left more than 70 percent of the Kurdish region without power. Omid Ahmed (also spelled Omed Ahmed), spokesperson for the Kurdistan Regional Government's Ministry of Electricity, said the attack suspended gas supply to power plants in Erbil, Sulaymaniyah, Bazian, Chamchamal, and Duhok, and knocked between 2,500 and 2,800 megawatts of generation off the grid, Al Jazeera reported, citing the official Iraqi News Agency (INA). Rudaw later quoted Ahmed as saying that authorities had increased generation from approximately 1,000 megawatts immediately after the attack to 1,550 megawatts, of which 50 megawatts were reserved for essential facilities and factories, leaving 1,500 megawatts for residents and raising daily public electricity supply to six to eight hours, reaching nine hours in some areas. Ahmed said the electricity then available covered only 40 percent of the region's demand, leaving a 60 percent shortfall, and that no date had been established for production to resume. Rudaw's article image assets for that report are dated Nov 13, 2026. Dana Gas, in a Saturday statement reported by Rudaw, said the facility had sustained significant damage and that currently no amount of gas could be produced. Later reports, including The Thursday Times on Nov 15, 2026, and QC Intel's account that the field was still offline one week after the attack, likewise said production remained shut. No official customer count was given. No later official generation figure, public-supply-hours update, or official confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed was found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday, Nov 20.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. As of the latest official statements found, no date had been established for Khor Mor production to resume.
outages.updated: Nov 8–16, 2026 attack and aftermath: Al Jazeera Nov 9 citing Iraqi and Kurdish officials and INA; KRG electricity ministry figures via Rudaw (article image assets dated Nov 13); Dana Gas still-shut statement via Rudaw, The Thursday Times Nov 15, and QC Intel one-week-after account; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday, no later official generation figure or confirmation that Khor Mor production had resumed found

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Torez, Debaltseve, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy said a large regional outage beginning at 3:30 p.m. on Nov 19 had been restored by 3:20 a.m. on Nov 20, but that the situation remained difficult, with new morning outages and forced temporary cuts because of a capacity deficit. On Friday, the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as reported by MK Donbass, said a capacity deficit was being caused by damage to transmission networks and substations from UAV attacks, and that temporary outages were being used to avoid further accidents.
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, in a Nov 20 morning statement posted by DNR News at 12:36 (3:36 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), said that at 3:30 p.m. on Nov 19 an emergency in the regional power system had caused large-scale electricity outages, and that after repair and commissioning work, electricity supply to all consumers disconnected by that accident had been restored by 3:20 a.m. on Nov 20, including in Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Dokuchaievsk, and the Novoazovsk, Volodarske, and Volnovakha municipal districts. It said the situation in the power system remained difficult, that new supply disruptions were recorded on Friday morning for various reasons, and that new emergencies had been recorded in the Volnovakha, Volodarske, and Shakhtarsk municipal districts and in Yenakiieve and Khartsyzk. It said forced temporary outages because of a shortage of available capacity, and to prevent equipment overloads and new large-scale accidents, were partially affecting Donetsk, Makiivka, Torez, Snizhne, and the Shakhtarsk and Amvrosiivka municipal districts, and that repair work accompanied by temporary outages was under way in Ilovaisk and some settlements in Horlivka. MK, in a Friday, Nov 20 report timed at 12:33 (3:33 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), cited Donetsk occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin as saying that more than 20,000 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk. MK quoted Kulemzin as saying that in Donetsk's Proletarskyi district, 72 transformer substations had been de-energized and 19,544 subscribers remained without electricity, and that in the Leninskyi district, 31 transformer substations had been partially de-energized because the network load had exceeded the allowable limit, leaving 3,550 subscribers without power. Kulemzin said work to restore electricity supply was under way. Those Friday morning city figures were not presented as a region-wide total covering Makiivka, Mariupol, and other cities. A later Kulemzin statement, posted by DNR News, said that according to Donetskenergo, six transformer substations in the Leninskyi district had automatically tripped, leaving 872 subscribers without electricity, and that restoration work was under way. That later statement did not give a remaining figure for the Proletarskyi district or a later citywide total. No independently confirmed customer count, and no later official region-wide remaining total, was found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as reported by RIA Novosti at 1:16 p.m. Moscow time Thursday, Nov 19 (4:16 a.m. CT), said supply would be restored to consumers in stages as damage was repaired, the system stabilized, and technical possibility appeared. The later Thursday-afternoon ministry update, reported by RIA Novosti at 5:52 p.m. Moscow time Thursday (8:52 a.m. CT), did not give a firm restoration time. That is not an official firm restoration time.
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy via DNR News 12:36 Friday (= 3:36 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on restoration by 3:20 a.m. of the Nov 19 regional accident and on Friday morning forced temporary outages; occupation city head Aleksey Kulemzin via MK 12:33 Friday (= 3:33 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on more than 20,000 subscribers remaining without power in Donetsk, including 19,544 in Proletarskyi district and 3,550 in Leninskyi district; later Kulemzin statement via DNR News on 872 subscribers remaining in Leninskyi district after six substations tripped; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday, no later official region-wide remaining total found

outages.cause: Occupation utility Krymenergo said Friday, Nov 20, that additional electricity-consumption restrictions had been introduced and that Alushta and Sudak had been completely de-energized for urgent network repairs. A later Friday evening Krymenergo statement, reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, said restrictions were still leaving 103 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy, and the settlements of Izumrudnoye and Luganskoye, without power, for a period of approximately three hours. Occupation authorities, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, have said a power deficit on the peninsula began after Oct 24 attacks on transmission networks outside the peninsula, which those sources attributed to Ukrainian drones; that attribution was not independently confirmed
outages.affected: No official customer count was given. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a report published at 12:40 p.m. and updated at 12:45 p.m. Friday, Nov 20 (3:40 a.m. and 3:45 a.m. CT if the times are Moscow time), citing Krymenergo, said that on Friday afternoon additional restrictions on electricity-consumption regimes had been introduced, and that residents of 12 districts, five urban districts, and two cities would be without power for three to six hours. It listed the de-energized districts as Bakhchysarai, Bilohirsk, Kirovske, Dzhankoi, Krasnohvardiiske, Lenine, Pervomaiske, Nyzhnohirskyi, Rozdolne, Saky, Simferopol, and Sovietskyi, and said there was also no power in the urban districts of Simferopol, Yevpatoria, Kerch, Feodosia, and Yalta and in the cities of Saki and Dzhankoi. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a 1:38 p.m. Friday report (4:38 a.m. CT if the time is Moscow time) also citing Krymenergo, said Alushta and Sudak had been completely left without electricity on Friday because of urgent repair work on the networks, quoting Krymenergo as saying electricity supply had been disconnected in the Alushta and Sudak urban districts in connection with urgent repair work. RIA Novosti Crimea, in a later report published at 10:52 p.m. Friday, Nov 20 (1:52 p.m. CT if the time is Moscow time), citing Krymenergo, said that late Friday evening in Dzhankoy, 103 streets and lanes remained without power, and that the settlements of Izumrudnoye and Luganskoye were also de-energized. It quoted Krymenergo as saying that in connection with the introduced restrictions, electricity supply would be absent, and that the disconnection time was approximately three hours. It said supply was restricted on 71 streets and 33 lanes and dead-ends in Dzhankoy. If that approximately three-hour window is counted from the 10:52 p.m. Friday report time, it would have ended around 1:52 a.m. Saturday Moscow time, or 4:52 p.m. CT Friday, which is before this update; the report itself did not state a clock start or end time. Occupation sources, as summarized in the earlier RIA Novosti Crimea reports, have said interruptions in Crimea and Sevastopol began on Oct 24, when they said drones attacked transmission networks outside the peninsula, and that a further attack on energy facilities affecting the peninsula was made on the night of Nov 4; those accounts and attributions come from occupation sources and were not independently confirmed. No official customer count or firm restoration time was given. An evening Friday recheck at 6:00 PM CT Friday found no later official customer count, no official restoration notice for the complete outage in Alushta and Sudak, and no official confirmation that the Friday afternoon peninsula-wide 3-to-6-hour restrictions remained in effect into Saturday.
outages.start: Occupation sources said peninsula-wide interruptions began Oct 24, 2026; Friday's additional restrictions, the complete outage in Alushta and Sudak, and the later Friday evening Dzhankoy restrictions were reported Nov 20, 2026
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. Krymenergo, as reported by RIA Novosti Crimea, said Friday afternoon's additional restrictions would leave residents without power for three to six hours, and that the later Friday evening restrictions in Dzhankoy and in Izumrudnoye and Luganskoye were for approximately three hours. No duration was given for the complete outage in Alushta and Sudak beyond the statement that it was for urgent network repairs.
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 10:52 p.m. Friday (= 1:52 p.m. CT if Moscow time) on 103 streets and lanes in Dzhankoy plus Izumrudnoye and Luganskoye, for approximately three hours; Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 12:40 p.m. Friday, updated 12:45 p.m. Friday (= 3:40 a.m. and 3:45 a.m. CT if Moscow time), on additional 3-to-6-hour restrictions in 12 districts, five urban districts, and two cities; Krymenergo via RIA Novosti Crimea 1:38 p.m. Friday (= 4:38 a.m. CT if Moscow time) on Alushta and Sudak being completely de-energized for urgent network repairs; rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday, no later official customer count, no official restoration notice for Alushta and Sudak, and no official confirmation that the Friday afternoon peninsula-wide restrictions remained in effect into Saturday

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Friday bulletin said that unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance
outages.affected: UNE's Friday bulletin, published by Cubadebate on Friday, Nov 20, and also reported by Granma, Directorio Cubano, and Limonada 24/7 citing Cubadebate, is the latest official national forecast found: if forecast conditions hold, 1,835 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,045 MW available versus 2,850 MW of demand (a 1,805 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Friday (5:00 a.m. CT), the grid had 1,000 MW available versus 2,250 MW of demand, leaving 1,242 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,350 MW affected at midday. On Thursday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning Friday; the maximum Thursday affectation was 1,789 MW at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Thursday (5:50 p.m. CT Thursday). Thursday solar photovoltaic output was 4,320 MWh, with a maximum of 672 MW. The Friday bulletin said unit 8 of CTE Mariel, unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, unit 1 of CTE Felton, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance. It said thermal generation limitations were 368 MW, and that unit 8 of Mariel was expected to enter at the evening peak with 45 MW. Official UNE sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. The Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, as compiled by CiberCuba, reported at 6:00 p.m. Cuba time Friday, Nov 20 (5:00 p.m. CT) that 147 distribution circuits were affected and that the affectation was 330 MW, due to a generation deficit. At that same hour it reported outage durations on individual Havana circuits, including 10 hours and 23 minutes on circuit PG980 in Arroyo Naranjo, 5 hours and 25 minutes on circuit GC15 in Guanabacoa, and multi-hour outages on circuits in San Miguel del Padrón, Diez de Octubre, Plaza, Playa, Marianao, and Regla. Those Havana circuit figures are not an official nationwide evening-peak actual. No official Friday evening-peak actual from UNE was found as of 6:00 PM CT Friday (6:00 p.m. Cuba time is 5:00 p.m. CT; this update is 6:00 p.m. CT, or 7:00 p.m. Cuba time), when the evening peak period was underway.
outages.updated: Nov 20, 2026, Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana 6:00 p.m. Cuba time Friday (= 5:00 p.m. CT) via CiberCuba, 147 circuits and 330 MW affected in Havana; UNE Friday bulletin via Cubadebate and Granma, figures as of 6:00 a.m. Cuba time Friday (= 5:00 a.m. CT), including the official Thursday evening-peak actual of 1,789 MW at 6:50 p.m. Cuba time Thursday (= 5:50 p.m. CT Thursday); rechecked 6:00 PM CT Friday, no official Friday evening-peak actual from UNE found

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. It said the strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water, and food production. AFP, in a Nov 17 report on the same OHCHR findings, likewise said the intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a worrying trend, and quoted the report as saying that between Oct 20 and Nov 4 some 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. That official humanitarian account is later than an Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature, which said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. Al Jazeera said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours.
